layer1_philosophy.methodology: A flexible home-education design guide, not a prescribed boxed curriculum. It gives public-school comparison points and extensive resources by grade and subject, then asks the parent to select, adapt, accelerate, delay, or replace them according to the actual child.
principles: Treat grade-level lists as a reference, never a verdict or lockstep requirement.
Tailor content and pace to the individual child and the family's setting.
Protect curiosity by following questions together and modeling how to find out.
Connect subjects because an interesting question can lead across the curriculum.
Use real books, practical life, experiments, art, movement, technology, and community resources alongside direct instruction.
Preschool belongs to play, conversation, read-alouds, household participation, outdoor exploration, and affection rather than formal curriculum.

layer1_philosophy.learningTheory: Curiosity-led, book-rich, interdisciplinary, experiential, developmentally flexible learning supported by explicit skills, rich resources, real-world practice, and parent-child inquiry.
layer1_philosophy.assessmentApproach: Use portfolios, conversations, demonstrations, writing, projects, informal observation, and legally required records. Compare against grade-level expectations as a planning aid, not a judgment of the child.
layer1_philosophy.parentRole: Curate resources, answer questions, say 'Let's find out' when the answer is unknown, notice interests and readiness, connect subjects, teach essential skills, and revise the plan when the child does not fit the nominal grade list.

knowledgeBankMatches.note: The source is a broad method and scope reference for designing a family-specific curriculum.
The book explicitly discusses natural or child-led learning, while also retaining planned skill and content expectations.

layer2_scope.coverage: Preschool, kindergarten, grades 1 through 8, a high-school overview, and grades 9 through 12 across language arts, mathematics, history and geography, science, foreign language, the arts, philosophy and comparative religion, health and physical education, life skills, and computer and technology skills.
layer2_scope.progression: The same subject families recur at each grade while expectations, independence, abstraction, reading difficulty, mathematical content, scientific inquiry, cultural reach, and technology use deepen.
layer2_scope.mappingNotes: This is a broad scope reference rather than a catalog of atomic Homa topics. Its grade-by-subject headings map to existing subject domains; no new taxonomy node is justified by the book's organizational labels.

layer3_structure.yearShape: Fourteen developmental bands from preschool through grade twelve, plus introductory chapters on educational choices, interdisciplinary connection, general subject principles, assessment, records, and multimedia learning.
layer3_structure.unitPattern: Each grade chapter opens with developmental context, then moves subject by subject through expected skills, possible content, recommended books, programs, websites, films, kits, and practical activities.
layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: No universal weekly schedule is prescribed. Build a family rhythm from short skill practice, sustained reading, discussion, projects, experiments, arts, movement, practical life, and interest-led extensions.
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: Revisit reading, writing, mathematics, inquiry, physical competence, life skills, and technology every year while expanding independence and complexity.
layer3_structure.pacingNotes: The nominal grade is an index into possibilities. The parent should move across adjacent chapters when the learner's readiness or interest differs from the average sequence.

activityTypes.description: Select goals and resources across the recurring subject headings for one learner's year.
Build a reading life from picture books, literature, nonfiction, magazines, and recommended lists.
Review age-typical skills warmly and use the result to choose practice without turning it into a verdict.
Learn through experiments, building, cooking, gardening, crafts, field trips, and practical household work.

activityTypes.description: Record direct outdoor observations with simple maps, pictures, labels, and notes.

layer5_lessons.notes: The book's learner-facing grain is the grade-band chapter, not a paced lesson. Each row preserves that complete chapter sequence; named resource lists remain searchable in the full sidecar rather than being misrepresented as assigned lessons.
